title: STRANGE MINUTE #23

lines.text: What if the space station fell out of the sky?
The ISS is as long as a football field and weighs about 925,000 pounds.
lines.say: The I.S.S. is as long as a football field and weighs about nine hundred twenty-five thousand pounds.

lines.text: It flies 250 miles up, at 17,500 miles per hour.
lines.say: It flies two hundred fifty miles up, at seventeen thousand five hundred miles per hour.

lines.text: Fast enough to see about 16 sunrises every single day.
lines.say: Fast enough to see about sixteen sunrises every single day.

lines.text: But even up there, there's a tiny bit of air, slowly dragging it down.
Without engine boosts, it would sink, and fall.
And that's actually the plan. Around 2030, it's being retired.
lines.say: And that's actually the plan. Around twenty thirty, it's being retired.

lines.text: A special SpaceX tug will push it down on purpose.
Most of it will burn up, a fireball streaking across the sky.
The rest splashes into the most remote patch of the Pacific.
Last time a station fell uncontrolled, in 1979, Skylab hit Australia.
lines.say: Last time a station fell uncontrolled, in nineteen seventy-nine, Skylab hit Australia.

lines.text: One town even fined NASA 400 dollars for littering.
lines.say: One town even fined NASA four hundred dollars for littering.

lines.text: So, should we let it fall, or keep it up there as a museum?

sources: NASA: ISS ~ 109 m long (football field incl. end zones), ~420,000 kg ≈ 925,000 lb, ~250 mi altitude, ~17,500 mph, ~16 sunrises/day
